Most-specific-wins (har node par marker, poora path walk, deepest marker jeete) defensible hai, par usme dono tries complete walk karne padte, comparison code aata, aur 'narrow allow baad mein add hue broad block se haar gaya' jaisa confusing support case banta. Naya feature add karte waqt ek existing, tested precedence contract chupchaap badalna galat hoga -- woh alag, explicit decision hona chahiye.
why_needed: Interviewer dekhna chahta hai ki candidate jo ACTUALLY bana hai (allow-always-wins, do instances) aur jo abhi bhi missing hai (blocklists ke beech precedence) ko clearly alag kar sakta hai, aur ek naya feature existing contract tode bina design kar sakta hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek office jahan ek VIP guest list hai (allowlist) jo har ban list ko override karti hai -- naam VIP list par hai toh andar, baat khatam. Ab agar do ban lists ho jaayein (security team ki strict list, HR ki relaxed list), toh unke beech ka order sirf yeh decide karta hai ki rokne wala kaunsa reason likha jaaye ya kaunsa rasta dikhaya jaaye -- VIP list ka rule waisa hi rehta hai.
how_it_works: Aaj: allowList?.isBlocked(name) ek trie walk; true ho toh blockList ka walk hota hi nahi. Proposed extension: allowlist check same rahe, phir `for (const b of this.blockLists) if (b.list.isBlocked(name)) return this.buildBlockResponse(base, q, b)` -- pehli matching list ka mode/naam use ho. Har list apna trie rakhti hai, isliye BlockList class mein ek line bhi nahi badalti; precedence poori tarah caller (handle) ke array order mein hai, data structure mein nahi.
in_this_project: src/proxy.ts: `allowList?: BlockList` SinkholeProxyOptions par optional hai, aur handle() mein `allowed` computation + `!allowed &&` guard hi poora Stage 2 hai. src/blocklist.ts ka BlockList allowlist ke liye bina kisi change ke reuse hua. test/proxy.test.ts ka "allowlist (Stage 2)" describe block dono directions prove karta hai: 'safe.ads.example.com' allowed + 'ads.example.com' blocked -> forward, aur 'example.com' allowed + 'ads.example.com' blocked -> bhi forward ('allowlist wins unconditionally, not by specificity'). Multiple blocklists ka code repo mein nahi hai.
advantages: BlockList class untouched rehti hai -- har nayi list sirf ek aur instance hai, trie code ka risk zero
Allow-always-wins ek single short-circuit hai, explain karna aur test karna dono aasaan
Blocklists ke beech precedence ek ordered array hai -- config mein dikhta hai, code mein chhupa nahi
disadvantages: Har active blocklist ke liye ek alag trie walk -- N lists = N walks per non-allowed query (labels ki count tak bounded, par constant factor badhta)
Allow-always-wins 'broad allow ke andar ek sub-subdomain phir se block karo' express nahi kar sakta
Shared suffixes ab lists ke BEECH share nahi hote -- har trie apne nodes rakhta hai
common_mistakes: Yeh kehna ki allowlist abhi nahi hai -- Stage 2 mein bana hai; jo missing hai woh blocklists ke BEECH precedence hai
Multiple blocklists add karte waqt allowlist ko 'bhi ek list' bana ke order mein daal dena -- isse allow-always-wins chupchaap 'allow agar pehle aaye toh' ban jaata hai
Most-specific-wins ko 'obviously better' bolna bina uski cost (dono tries full walk, comparison code, confusing support cases) bataaye
follow_up_questions: Agar product ko most-specific-wins chahiye hi ho, toh tum isBlocked() ke saath kya naya API add karoge (hint: deepest matching depth return karna)?
Ordered blocklists mein stats ko per-list kaise todoge bina ProxyStats ko bahut bada banaye?
Kaunsa test prove karega ki naya blocklist array allowlist ki precedence ko nahi todta?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Separate BlockList instances composed in handle() (chosen) vs one enriched trie with per-node markers: separate instances keep the trie code unchanged and put precedence where it is visible (caller order), at the cost of one walk per list; a single marker trie is one walk but makes BlockList know about meanings and forces a full-path walk for most-specific-wins.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar extension mein koi developer allowlist ko ordered list ka ek element bana de, ek allowlisted naam tab bhi block hoga jab koi blocklist array mein usse pehle aa jaaye -- silent behaviour change. Isliye test/proxy.test.ts ke 'allowlist wins unconditionally' tests ko har naye blocklist ke saath bhi pass hona chahiye.
advanced.alternatives: Most-specific-wins marker trie (PLAN.md mein considered aur rejected); ya ek priority number per entry jahan highest priority jeete (Adblock-style `@@` exceptions jaisa) -- flexible par config ko samajhna mushkil.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Lists ki sankhya 10x hone par per-query cost N walks ho jaati hai; tab sab lists ko ek merged trie mein compile karna (har node par 'kaunsi lists' ka bitmask) ek walk mein sab answer de sakta hai -- par yeh tab tak premature hai jab tak measurement na bole.
advanced.production_improvements: Per-list hit counters, list load ke waqt overlap report (kaun se entries ek doosre ko shadow kar rahi hain), aur ek explicit documented precedence policy README mein -- jaise Stage 2 ne allowlist ke liye kiya.

question: How would you add RFC 2308-style negative caching (caching NXDOMAIN/NODATA using the SOA record's TTL) the way 15-dns-resolver already does?
answer_hinglish:
Abhi handle() sirf `parsed.header.rcode === RCODE.NOERROR && parsed.answers.length > 0` hone par cache.put() karta hai -- matlab NXDOMAIN ya NODATA (NOERROR par zero answers) kabhi cache nahi hota, har identical query dobara upstream ko jaati hai. PLAN.md explicitly yeh gap document karta hai, aur ek important detail bhi: `Math.min(...parsed.answers.map(...))` jab answers.length === 0 ho, `Math.min()` bina arguments ke `Infinity` return karta hai (throw nahi karta) -- isliye guard zaroori hai, warna 'koi answer nahi' aur 'infinite TTL' confuse ho jaate.

Negative caching add karne ke liye, authority section mein SOA record ka MINIMUM field (last field, jo negative-caching TTL hota hai RFC 2308 ke mutabiq) decode karna padega. Abhi decodeResponse authority section bilkul NAHI padhta ('Authority/additional are not read at all'). Toh pehla step: decodeResponse ko EXTEND karna hoga nscount bhi parse kare, aur authority records mein SOA type dhoondhe, uske rdata ke andar se MINIMUM field nikaale (yeh rdata ke andar hai, toh yahan EK CHHOTI exception banani padegi 'never decode rdata' rule mein -- sirf SOA ka MINIMUM field, jo fixed-position hai SOA rdata ke end mein, bina kisi compressed name ko touch kiye).

Phir cache.put() ko ek NAYA path add karna hoga: rcode === NXDOMAIN ya (NOERROR with zero answers), SOA mila, uska MINIMUM TTL se cache karo. 15-dns-resolver already yeh pattern implement karta hai, toh yeh 'same idea, not a new design problem' hai jaisa PLAN.md khud kehta hai.
why_needed: Interviewer dekhna chahta hai ki candidate RFC 2308 negative caching samajhta hai, aur yeh bhi ki is project ke 'never decode rdata' principle se ek CAREFUL, SCOPED exception kaise banayi jaaye bina overall design ko compromise kiye.
real_world_analogy: Ek dukaan jo har 'yeh item stock mein nahi hai' jawab bhi thodi der ke liye YAAD rakhti hai (jaise 'is item ko 5 minute tak dobara mat poochna, hum jaante hain abhi stock mein nahi hai') -- bajaye har baar warehouse ko phir se call karne ke sirf 'NAHI' sunne ke liye.
how_it_works: SOA rdata ka format hai: MNAME, RNAME (compressed names possible), phir 5 fixed 32-bit integers (serial, refresh, retry, expire, MINIMUM) -- MINIMUM last field hai aur RFC 2308 ke mutabiq negative-caching TTL ke liye use hota hai. Isko padhne ke liye MNAME/RNAME ko SKIP karna padega (unke names ko readName se traverse karna, jo compression handle karta hai) phir fixed 20 bytes (5 x 4-byte integers) padhna hai, last 4 bytes MINIMUM hain.
in_this_project: src/wire.ts ka decodeResponse abhi sirf `nscount` ko padh ke IGNORE kar deta hai (r.u16("nscount") call hoti hai par us count se koi record padha nahi jaata). src/proxy.ts ka handle() cache.put() call sirf NOERROR+answers.length>0 guard ke peeche hai.
advantages: Repeated NXDOMAIN queries (jaise typo domains ya malware callbacks) upstream ko hit nahi karenge
15-dns-resolver mein already proven pattern hai, same idea reuse ho sakta hai
disadvantages: decodeResponse ko authority section parse karna padega -- scope thoda badhta hai

SOA rdata ke andar jaana ek CAREFUL, scoped exception hai 'never decode rdata' rule mein -- har future developer ko yeh samajhna padega ki yeh exception KYUN safe hai (no compression pointer touched, only fixed fields after two names)
common_mistakes: Guard (`answers.length > 0`) ko hata dena bina negative caching add kiye -- Math.min() Infinity return karega aur response EFFECTIVELY forever cache ho jaayega

SOA record ke MNAME/RNAME ko skip karne ke liye readName use NA karna -- yeh names compressed ho sakte hain, rdlength se simple skip unhe sahi se handle nahi karega agar unke baad ke fixed fields ka offset calculate karna ho
follow_up_questions: Why is reading the SOA's MINIMUM field a safer exception to the 'never decode rdata' rule than decoding a CNAME's target?
What would happen today if the answers.length > 0 guard were removed?
How would you cache a negative result separately from a positive one for the same (name, type) key?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Negative caching adds real value (reduces repeated failed lookups) but requires carefully scoping the rdata-decoding exception to SOA's fixed trailing fields only -- a broader rdata decoder would reintroduce the compression-pointer risk this project avoids everywhere else.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar MINIMUM field ko galat offset se padha jaaye (jaise MNAME/RNAME compression ko sahi se skip na kiya), negative-cache TTL GALAT number ban jaayega -- ya toh bahut chhota (cache useless) ya bahut bada (stale negative result bahut der tak serve hoga, jaise ek domain jo abhi register hua hai woh phir bhi NXDOMAIN dikhega purani cache se).
advanced.alternatives: Ek simpler, less-correct approach: NXDOMAIN ko ek FIXED short TTL (jaise 30 seconds) se cache karna bina SOA MINIMUM parse kiye -- less accurate (RFC-non-compliant) par much simpler, zero rdata decoding chahiye.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: High query volume par negative caching ka benefit BADH jaata hai -- repeated failed lookups (typos, malware beaconing to dead domains) ek significant fraction ho sakte hain traffic ka, aur unhe cache karna upstream load kaafi kam kar sakta hai.
advanced.production_improvements: SOA-based negative caching implement karne ke baad, ek SEPARATE stats counter (negativeCacheHits) add karo taaki production mein pata chale yeh feature kitna effective hai, aur SOA parsing ke liye dedicated fuzz tests likho jaise existing wire.ts tests karte hain.

question: How would you add request coalescing so that N concurrent identical queries for the same (name, type) result in only ONE upstream call?
answer_hinglish:
Abhi agar 50 clients EK SAME SAATH 'news.example.com' A record poochte hain (jaise ek popular site ka cold cache), har ek apna SEPARATE forwardQuery() call trigger karega, apna ALAG ephemeral socket, apna ALAG upstream round-trip -- 50 identical upstream queries, sirf isliye kyunki unke beech koi COORDINATION nahi hai.

Request coalescing ka idea: ek in-memory `Map<string, Promise<Buffer>>` rakho (key = canonicalName + type, SAME key jo cache use karta hai). Jab handle() ek NON-cached query process kare, PEHLE yeh map check karo -- agar SAME key ke liye already ek in-flight forward Promise chal raha hai, usi Promise ko AWAIT karo bajaye NAYA forwardQuery() start karne ke. Jab woh Promise resolve ho, SABHI waiting callers ko SAME result milega (par har ek apna OWN transaction id patch karega -- yeh already patchId() se possible hai).

Important detail: coalescing sirf UPSTREAM CALL ko share karta hai, HAR CLIENT ko apna khud ka transaction-id-patched response milna chahiye -- toh Promise resolve hone ke baad, har caller apna patchId(result, ownId) karega. Map entry ko Promise ke settle (resolve YA reject) hone par IMMEDIATELY delete karna zaroori hai (`.finally()` block), warna agle genuine-new query ko ek STALE promise mil jaayegi.
why_needed: Interviewer dekhna chahta hai ki candidate 'thundering herd' problem ko identify kar sakta hai aur ek PRACTICAL, Map-based coalescing solution design kar sakta hai, including cleanup correctness (finally block).
real_world_analogy: Ek hi restaurant table ke 10 log SAME dish order karte hain ek saath -- kitchen ek hi baar banayegi aur SABKO serve karegi, bajaye 10 baar SEPARATE banane ke.
how_it_works: Coalescing Map ki key SAME honi chahiye jo cache use karta hai (canonicalName + type), taaki EXACTLY woh queries jo SAME cache entry banayengi, coalesce ho. Promise ko map mein DAALNE ka time matters -- forwardQuery() CALL karne se PEHLE map mein daalo, taaki race condition na ho (do queries EK SAME tick par aayen).
in_this_project: src/proxy.ts ka handle() abhi directly `await forwardQuery(...)` karta hai har non-cached query ke liye -- coalescing map ko is call ke AROUND wrap karna hoga, SinkholeProxy class mein ek naya private field (jaise `inFlight: Map<string, Promise<Buffer>>`) add karke.
advantages: Thundering-herd ko eliminate karta hai -- upstream load N se 1 tak drop ho sakta hai popular cold-cache queries ke liye
Map-based approach simple hai, existing cache-key scheme reuse kar sakta hai
disadvantages: Har coalesced caller ko SAME transaction id wala raw response milta hai jab tak patchId() apply na ho -- yeh extra step zaroori hai

Agar EK caller ki query thodi DIFFERENT ho (jaise alag 'rd' flag) par SAME (name, type) ho, coalescing unko same upstream response de dega jo subtly INCORRECT ho sakta hai depending on kya differ karta hai
common_mistakes: Promise ko map se delete karna sirf SUCCESS case mein -- agar forward FAIL ho (SERVFAIL case), map mein stale rejected promise reh jaayegi agle genuine attempt ke liye jab tak explicitly cleanup na ho
Coalescing ko CACHE ke bajaye BLOCKLIST check ke saath bhi apply karne ki koshish karna -- blocklist check already instant hai (no I/O), coalescing ki zaroorat sirf upstream-bound calls ke liye hai
follow_up_questions: Why must the in-flight map entry be removed in a .finally() rather than only on success?
What happens if two coalesced callers have different original transaction IDs?
Could coalescing accidentally merge two queries that should get different answers?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: In-memory Map-based coalescing hai simple aur single-process-scoped -- ek multi-instance deployment mein (agar kabhi horizontally scale kiya jaaye) har instance apna ALAG coalescing karega, cross-instance coalescing ke liye shared state (Redis jaisa) chahiye hoga.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar cleanup (.finally()) miss ho jaaye ek edge case mein (jaise an uncaught synchronous throw before the promise is even created), map mein stale entry reh sakti hai jo FOREVER future queries ko block kar degi us key ke liye -- ek subtle, hard-to-notice production bug.
advanced.alternatives: Ek alternative hai 'leader election per key' pattern jahan explicitly ek caller 'leader' banta hai aur baaki 'followers' -- functionally similar par zyada explicit state machine, is scale ke liye overkill.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Coalescing ka benefit traffic SPIKES mein sabse zyada dikhta hai (jaise sab devices ek saath boot hote hain) -- 10x/100x normal steady-state traffic mein benefit kam hoga kyunki queries naturally spread out honge, par BURST scenarios mein yeh upstream load ko dramatically kam karta hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Coalescing hit count ko ek NAYA stats counter mein track karo (kitni baar ek caller ko in-flight request join karna pada bajaye naya start karne ke) -- yeh batayega yeh optimization kitna effective hai real traffic patterns mein.

question: How would you add EDNS(0) passthrough to this proxy, given that OPT records currently live in the additional section this proxy never reads?
answer_hinglish:
EDNS(0) ek OPT pseudo-record hai jo DNS message ke ADDITIONAL section mein hota hai (arcount se count hota hai) -- yeh client/upstream ko bade UDP payload sizes (512 bytes se zyada) negotiate karne deta hai, aur DNSSEC jaise extensions ke liye flags carry karta hai. Abhi decodeQuery `arcount` ko padh ke IGNORE kar deta hai -- koi additional record actually parse nahi hota.

Sabse SIMPLE EDNS passthrough yeh hai: client ki query jo bhi additional records carry kare (including OPT), unhe UNTOUCHED relay karo upstream ko -- yeh ALREADY ho raha hai client-to-upstream direction mein, kyunki forwardQuery RAW query buffer forward karta hai, kabhi re-encode nahi karta! Toh client->upstream direction mein EDNS already 'passthrough' hai, bas iska EXPLICIT acknowledgment nahi hai.

Real gap hai UPSTREAM REPLY mein -- jab proxy decodeResponse karta hai, woh additional section bilkul nahi padhta (`arcount` read hota hai par uska data skip nahi hota explicitly, jo ek BUG hai agar additional records ke baad kuch aur expected ho). Fix: decodeResponse ko arcount records bhi skip karna chahiye (OPT ko samajhne ki zaroorat nahi, sirf length se skip karo jaise answers ke rdata), taaki relay complete reply bhejta rahe bina OPT ko drop kiye. Blocked/own-built responses (sinkhole, NXDOMAIN, FORMERR) mein OPT echo karna ek SEPARATE feature hoga -- abhi encodeMessage koi additional records nahi banata.
why_needed: Interviewer dekhna chahta hai ki candidate EDNS(0) ke basics samajhta hai (OPT pseudo-record, additional section), aur yeh bhi ki is proxy ke RAW-RELAY design mein EDNS passthrough actually kahan 'already working' hai aur kahan GAP hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek courier jo poora parcel deliver karta hai bina khole -- agar parcel ke andar ek EXTRA note (OPT jaisa) ho jo sender-to-receiver specific instruction carry kare, woh note bhi parcel ke saath jaata hai AUTOMATICALLY, jab tak courier beech mein parcel ko repack na kare.
how_it_works: decodeQuery/decodeResponse dono `arcount` ko read karte hain par uske records ko explicitly SKIP nahi karte -- yeh sirf tab problem hai jab buffer ke us hisse ko kisi NAYE packet mein copy karna ho (jo client->upstream direction mein already raw-relay se automatically solve hai, par upstream->client decoded-then-relay mein bhi raw relay hi hai, toh yeh bhi automatically theek hai!).
in_this_project: src/wire.ts ka decodeQuery aur decodeResponse dono `r.u16("arcount")` call karte hain par is value ko actually kahin use nahi karte -- yeh ek 'parsed but ignored' field hai. src/proxy.ts ka handle() forward path mein poora replyBuf (jisme OPT bhi ho sakta hai) raw relay hota hai, toh EDNS already 'accidentally passthrough' hai successful-forward case mein.
advantages: Client-to-upstream aur successful-upstream-to-client EDNS passthrough already 'free' hai is raw-relay design ki wajah se
Koi naya OPT-parsing code client/upstream flow ke liye zaroori nahi
disadvantages: Proxy-built responses (block mode, SERVFAIL, FORMERR) EDNS buffer-size signal ko IGNORE karte hain -- agar client ne bada UDP buffer size negotiate kiya tha, proxy ka chhota built response us negotiation ko respect nahi karta (though practically harmless, kyunki proxy ke built responses chhote hi hote hain)
DNSSEC-related EDNS flags (jaise DO bit) ka koi special handling nahi hai
common_mistakes: Yeh sochna ki EDNS support 'poora missing' hai -- actually successful forward path mein yeh already kaam karta hai, sirf proxy-built responses mein gap hai
OPT record ko fully PARSE karne ki koshish karna jab sirf PASSTHROUGH chahiye -- passthrough ke liye parse karne ki zaroorat hi nahi, raw relay kaafi hai
follow_up_questions: Why does EDNS passthrough already work for the successful-forward path without any extra code?
What would it take to echo an OPT record back on a proxy-built NXDOMAIN response?
Would you ever need to actually parse OPT's content, rather than just relay it?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Raw-relay design incidentally gives EDNS passthrough for free on the common path -- a fully-decoding proxy would need explicit OPT-record support, which is extra encoder/decoder work this design sidesteps entirely.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar koi client EDNS buffer size negotiate karta hai aur proxy ek block response bina OPT echo kiye bhejta hai, client shayad default 512-byte assumption par fall back kare -- practically harmless yahan kyunki proxy ke built responses chhote hain, par ek doosre context mein yeh problem ban sakta tha.
advanced.alternatives: Full EDNS support (OPT parsing, DO bit handling for DNSSEC) -- zaroori hoga agar yeh proxy kabhi DNSSEC validation jaisa feature add kare, par abhi iski zaroorat nahi hai is proxy ke scope mein.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: EDNS passthrough ka traffic-volume se koi relation nahi hai -- yeh ek per-packet correctness concern hai, throughput-independent.
advanced.production_improvements: Agar block responses ke liye bhi EDNS-aware behavior chahiye ho, encodeMessage ko ek optional OPT-echo parameter diya ja sakta hai jo client ki query se OPT record (agar present ho) copy kare apne built response mein -- scope-limited addition, poora EDNS parser nahi chahiye.

question: How would you add AAAA sinkholing (answering a blocked AAAA query with :: instead of NXDOMAIN) without breaking the existing A-record sinkhole path?
answer_hinglish:
Abhi buildBlockResponse ek single condition check karta hai: `if (this.mode === "nxdomain" || q.type !== TYPE.A) return NXDOMAIN`. Matlab sinkhole mode mein bhi, AAAA query NXDOMAIN hi paata hai, kyunki condition explicitly `q.type !== TYPE.A` ko NXDOMAIN branch mein daal deta hai.

AAAA sinkholing add karne ke liye, do kaam chahiye honge: (1) ek `encodeAAAARecord(name, ttl, address)` function likhna wire.ts mein, jo IPv6 address ko 16 bytes mein encode kare (encodeARecord jaisa hi structure, bas TYPE.AAAA aur 16-byte address ke saath, IPv6 parsing/validation ke saath jo IPv4 se zyada complex hai -- colons, double-colon shorthand, etc.). (2) buildBlockResponse ke condition ko EXTEND karna: `q.type !== TYPE.A && q.type !== TYPE.AAAA` NXDOMAIN branch mein, aur ek naya branch jo q.type check kare aur A ke liye encodeARecord, AAAA ke liye encodeAAAARecord call kare apne respective sinkhole addresses (jaise A ke liye '0.0.0.0', AAAA ke liye '::') ke saath.

Yeh EXISTING A-record path ko NAHI todta kyunki hum sirf condition ko BROADEN kar rahe hain (ek aur case add kar rahe), existing A-record branch same rehta hai. SinkholeProxyOptions mein ek naya field `sinkholeAddressV6` (default '::') add karna hoga, jo sinkholeAddress (IPv4) se independent hoga.
why_needed: Interviewer dekhna chahta hai ki candidate ek EXISTING conditional ko SAFELY extend kar sakta hai additional case ke liye, aur IPv6 encoding ki specific complexity (address parsing) ko bhi acknowledge karta hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek dukaan jo abhi sirf EK language mein 'band hai' bolti hai -- doosri language add karna matlab ek ALAG translation add karna, par 'band hai' ka core message same rehta hai, aur pehli language wala sign kabhi nahi badalta.
how_it_works: encodeARecord ipv4ToBytes() helper use karta hai jo 4 dot-separated numbers parse karta hai. encodeAAAARecord ko IPv6 ka colon-separated hex-group format parse karna hoga, including '::' shorthand (jo consecutive zero groups ko compress karta hai) -- yeh ipv4ToBytes se significantly zyada complex parsing hai.
in_this_project: src/proxy.ts ka buildBlockResponse method aur src/wire.ts ka encodeARecord (jiske pattern ko encodeAAAARecord follow karega) yeh change ke primary touch points honge. TYPE.AAAA already wire.ts ke TYPE constant mein defined hai (value 28), sirf uska encoder missing hai.
advantages: Existing A-record sinkhole path untouched -- naya branch ADD hota hai, replace nahi
PLAN.md ne already yeh exact feature 'Candidates if ever picked up' mein list kiya hai -- scope-approved extension
disadvantages: IPv6 address parsing (colon groups, :: shorthand, embedded IPv4) A-record IPv4 parsing se significantly zyada complex hai
Ek naya config option (sinkholeAddressV6) API surface badhata hai
common_mistakes: Yeh sochna ki AAAA aur A record encoding bas 'address length' mein differ karte hain -- IPv6 PARSING (text-to-bytes) khud zyada complex hai, encoding (bytes-to-wire) relatively similar hai
Condition ko galat order mein likhna (jaise `q.type !== TYPE.AAAA` bhool jaana) -- isse A-record case accidentally NXDOMAIN branch mein chala jaayega
follow_up_questions: What makes IPv6 text-to-bytes parsing more complex than IPv4's?
Would you add a separate sinkholeAddressV6 option, or derive it automatically from sinkholeAddress?
What test would you write to prove the existing A-record sinkhole path still works after this change?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Extending the existing type-check condition keeps the change small and localized; a bigger refactor (a type-to-encoder map/registry) would scale better if MORE record types needed sinkholing later, but is more change for just one more type today.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar IPv6 parsing bug ho (jaise '::' shorthand galat expand ho), sinkhole response ek WRONG IPv6 address bhej sakta hai -- client us address ko try karega aur fail hoga differently from the intended 'go nowhere' sinkhole behavior, possibly leaking to an unintended real address.
advanced.alternatives: Ek registry pattern (`Map<number, (name, ttl, addr) => Buffer>`) jo query type ko encoder function se map kare -- future record types add karna easier banata, par abhi sirf EK type add karna hai, toh yeh over-engineering hoga.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Yeh feature traffic volume se independent hai -- har AAAA query ko ek extra branch check lagega, negligible cost regardless of scale.
advanced.production_improvements: IPv6 address parsing ke liye extensive fuzz/round-trip tests likho (jaisa encodeARecord ke liye already hain), specifically '::' shorthand, mixed IPv4-in-IPv6 notation, aur invalid-address rejection cases cover karte hue.

question: This project's mutation testing found 3 checks that were 'caught' only because of an unrelated check, or never actually exercised. Walk through one of these (WIRE5, TRANSPORT1, or PROXY3) and explain how the test suite was fixed to genuinely exercise it.
answer_hinglish:
Teeno ka pattern same hai: '89 tests pass ho rahe hain' (Stage 1 ke end par) yeh NAHI prove karta ki har individual guard genuinely exercise ho rahi hai. Mujhe TRANSPORT1 lete hain example ke roop mein -- yeh check hai `queryUdp` ka wrong-source-address/port filter (`if (rinfo.address !== to.host || rinfo.port !== to.port) return;`).

Mutation testing mein, jab yeh check DELIBERATELY remove kiya gaya (har reply accept karo, address check kiye bina), suite STILL PASS hua -- matlab is check ko hatane se KOI test fail nahi hua. Reason: har existing test mein, 'upstream' (StubUpstream) hi EKMATRA cheez thi jo kabhi reply bhejti thi -- koi DOOSRA sender kabhi exist hi nahi karta tha jiska reply filter ho sake. Check ke paas kuch 'filter karne ko' hi nahi tha, isliye uska absent hona bhi invisible rehta.

Isko HONESTLY close karne ke liye, ek test-only hook `ForwardOptions.onUdpBound` add kiya gaya -- yeh callback humare apne ephemeral UDP source port ko EXPOSE karta hai bind hone ke turant baad, real query bhejne se PEHLE. Naya test ek 'rogue socket' banata hai jo is hook ka use karke ek FULLY-FORMED, DIFFERENT spoofed answer hamare socket ko bhejta hai -- real upstream se bhi PEHLE. Test assert karta hai ki real upstream ka answer hi jeetta hai, rogue wala IGNORE hota hai. Re-run karne par, yeh check ab GENUINELY caught hota hai mutation testing mein.
why_needed: Interviewer dekhna chahta hai ki candidate mutation testing ki METHODOLOGY samajhta hai -- specifically yeh ki 'test passes' aur 'test actually EXERCISES the guard' do ALAG cheezein hain, aur ek test-only hook design karne ka practical skill dikha sakta hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek fire alarm jo kabhi test nahi hua REAL fire ke saath -- woh 'installed' hai, par kya woh ACTUALLY kaam karta hai yeh pata nahi jab tak koi genuinely fire lagaye (controlled test) aur dekhe alarm bajta hai ya nahi.
how_it_works: Mutation testing process: EXACT text replacement karo src/ mein (ek guard disable karo), poora suite run karo, result note karo ('caught' agar koi test fail hua, 'not caught' agar sab pass rahe), phir file ko byte-for-byte restore karo. 'Not caught' result ek REAL test gap hai.
in_this_project: README.md ki 'Mutation checks' table mein TRANSPORT1, WIRE5, aur PROXY3 teeno 'not caught -> closed' marked hain. src/transport.ts ka ForwardOptions.onUdpBound exactly is TRANSPORT1 gap ko close karne ke liye add kiya gaya test-only hook hai.
advantages: Mutation testing REAL confidence deta hai ki 'test passing' = 'guard actually working', na ki coincidental overlap
onUdpBound jaisa test-only hook production code ko minimal footprint ke saath testable banata hai
disadvantages: Mutation testing ek MANUAL, time-consuming process hai is project mein (deliberate edit, run, restore, repeat) -- automated mutation-testing tools (jaise Stryker) yeh scale par automate kar sakte
common_mistakes: Yeh maan lena ki 89 (ab 97) PASSING tests ka matlab hai sab guards genuinely tested hain -- WIRE5/TRANSPORT1/PROXY3 teeno exactly PROVE karte hain yeh assumption galat ho sakta hai
Test-only hooks (onUdpBound jaisa) ko production path mein leave karna without clearly marking 'test-only' -- yeh accidentally misuse ho sakta hai
follow_up_questions: What is the difference between a test suite passing and a guard being genuinely exercised?
How would you systematically find other checks that might be 'caught' only incidentally?
Why is a test-only hook (onUdpBound) preferable to, say, exposing the socket object directly for testing?
Stage 2 ka ALLOW10 bhi survive hua -- woh in teeno jaisa real gap kyun nahi maana gaya?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Adding test-only hooks (onUdpBound) to production code is a deliberate trade-off: a small amount of test-support surface in exchange for genuinely testing a security-relevant guard that otherwise has no observable effect from outside the module.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Without closing these gaps, a future refactor could accidentally remove the wrong-source-address check (or the reserved-label-type check, or the id/QR verification) and NO test would catch it -- the bug would only surface in production, possibly as a real security exposure, not a test failure.
advanced.alternatives: An automated mutation-testing tool (e.g. Stryker for TypeScript) could run this process continuously in CI instead of a manual one-time pass -- more overhead to set up, but catches regressions on every future change, not just at this one point in time.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: This methodology concern doesn't scale with traffic -- it's about test-suite quality, not runtime performance. But a larger codebase with more guards would benefit MORE from automating this check, since manual mutation testing does not scale well with code size.
advanced.production_improvements: Set up automated mutation testing in CI so every future change is checked against this same standard, rather than relying on a one-time manual pass to stay valid as the code evolves.

question: How would you add a query-logging / stats page beyond the current in-memory ProxyStats counters, and what would you need to be careful about?
answer_hinglish:
Abhi ProxyStats sirf AGGREGATE counters rakhta hai (total/blocked/allowed/cacheHits/forwarded/servfail) -- koi PER-QUERY log nahi hai, matlab 'konsa domain kab query hua' kabhi record nahi hota. Ek query-log add karne ke liye, handle() ke andar, response return karne se PEHLE, ek log entry emit karni hogi: timestamp, query name, type, decision (blocked/cache-hit/forwarded/servfail, plus ek alag 'allowlist override' flag kyunki allowed exclusive outcome nahi hai), aur latency.

Careful rehna hai PRIVACY ke baare mein -- DNS queries ek user ki poori BROWSING HISTORY reveal karti hain (kaunsi sites woh visit kar raha hai). Ek query log, agar persist hota hai, ek SENSITIVE data store ban jaata hai -- retention policy (kitni der tak rakhna hai), access control (kaun dekh sakta hai), aur possibly anonymization (jaise client IP ko log na karna, ya hash karna) sochna zaroori hoga, specially agar yeh office/home network ke multiple users serve kar raha ho.

Performance-wise, HAR query ke liye synchronously disk/network par log likhna latency add karega handle()'s hot path mein. Behtar approach: ek IN-MEMORY ring buffer (fixed size, jaisa ResponseCache ka maxEntries pattern) ya ek async/batched write queue -- log entries accumulate karo memory mein, periodically FLUSH karo disk/external store ko, taaki har individual query ka response time affected na ho.
why_needed: Interviewer dekhna chahta hai ki candidate ek observability feature design kar sakta hai jo PRIVACY-SENSITIVE data (browsing history) ko responsibly handle kare, aur performance impact (hot-path latency) ko bhi consider kare.
real_world_analogy: Ek dukaan ka CCTV camera footage -- useful hai security ke liye, par retention policy (kitne din rakhna), kaun dekh sakta hai, aur customers ki privacy expectations sab consider karne padte hain, sirf 'record karo' nahi bolte.
how_it_works: handle() ke multiple return points hain (blocked, cache-hit, forwarded, servfail, aur early drops) -- ek centralized logging call har path se PEHLE guzarna chahiye, ya ek wrapper function jo handle() ko call kare aur result + metadata ko log kare, bina handle() ki internal logic ko touch kiye.
in_this_project: src/proxy.ts ka ProxyStats sirf aggregate counts deta hai, per-query detail nahi. handle() ke multiple exit points (return statements) har ek is naye logging ki integration point ban sakte hain, ya ek WRAPPING function jo handle() ko call kare bina usko modify kiye.
advantages: Wrapping handle() (rather than modifying it) keeps the core decision logic unchanged and testable in isolation
A ring-buffer or batched-write approach avoids adding latency to the hot path
disadvantages: A detailed query log is inherently sensitive data (browsing history) -- adds real privacy/compliance responsibility
The illustrative wrapper above can't easily tell WHICH decision branch was taken without refactoring handle() to expose that explicitly
common_mistakes: Logging every query synchronously to disk without batching -- directly adds I/O latency to the DNS response path, which users will feel as 'slow internet'
Storing full query logs indefinitely without a retention policy -- turns a debugging feature into a privacy liability
follow_up_questions: What would you log, and what would you deliberately NOT log, for privacy reasons?
How would you refactor handle() to cleanly expose which decision branch was taken, for logging purposes?
What retention policy would you set for a query log on a home network vs an office network?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: A wrapping approach keeps proxy.ts's core logic untouched but can only observe inputs/outputs and aggregate counters, not WHICH exact branch fired; refactoring handle() to explicitly return a decision tag would give richer logs at the cost of changing the core function's contract.
advanced.failure_scenarios: If query logging is added synchronously on the hot path and the log sink (disk, network) becomes slow or unavailable, every DNS query would be delayed or blocked behind a logging call that has nothing to do with DNS correctness -- a logging outage could look like a DNS outage.
advanced.alternatives: An async, fire-and-forget logging call (never awaited) avoids blocking the response, but risks losing log entries on process crash; a bounded in-memory ring buffer with periodic flush balances both durability and latency reasonably well.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: At 10x/100x query volume, a per-query synchronous log write would become a real bottleneck; a batched/buffered approach is what makes logging scale without becoming the new bottleneck.
advanced.production_improvements: Implement structured, batched logging with an explicit retention policy and, ideally, anonymized or hashed client identifiers rather than raw addresses, and make the logging sink's own failure mode (e.g., disk full) non-blocking for the DNS response path.

question: Write a function that computes the cache hit ratio from a SinkholeProxy's stats object.
answer_hinglish:
ProxyStats mein cacheHits, forwarded, aur servfail teeno counters hain jo 'cache-eligible' queries (matlab woh queries jo blocklist mein nahi thi, isliye cache check tak pahunchi) ko represent karte hain. blocked queries kabhi cache ko touch nahi karte, toh unhe denominator mein shaamil nahi karna chahiye -- warna ratio artificially deflate ho jaayega.

Function simple hai: `cacheHits / (cacheHits + forwarded + servfail)`. Zero-division guard zaroori hai agar abhi tak koi cache-eligible query hi nahi aayi (fresh proxy). Yeh function proxy.stats directly leta hai, koi internal state access nahi karta -- isliye SinkholeProxy ke kisi bhi instance ke saath use ho sakta hai, test ho ya production.

Iske use case: production monitoring (jaisa SINK-109/112 mein discuss hua), ya ek unit test jo assert kare ki repeated queries ka hit ratio expected range mein hai.
why_needed: Interviewer dekhna chahta hai ki candidate production-relevant metrics ko sahi DENOMINATOR ke saath compute kar sakta hai -- blocked queries ko galti se shaamil karna ek common mistake hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek dukaan ka 'repeat customer rate' -- naye customers (jo pehli baar aaye, 'forwarded') aur purane customers (jo wapas aaye, 'cache hit') dono count hote hain, par jo log dukaan mein kabhi ghuse hi nahi (blocked entry) unhe count nahi karte.
how_it_works: cacheHits, forwarded, aur servfail teeno counters sirf un queries par increment hote hain jo blocklist check PAAR kar gayi (blocked nahi thi) -- isliye yeh teen MIL kar 'cache-eligible' population banate hain, aur unme se kitne % cacheHits the yeh is function ka core calculation hai.
in_this_project: SinkholeProxy.stats object directly yeh fields expose karta hai (readonly ProxyStats) -- koi extra computation proxy ke andar nahi hai, ratio HAMESHA caller-side compute hota hai jaisa yeh function karta hai.
advantages: Correct denominator -- blocked queries never hit the cache, so they are excluded
Pure function, no side effects, trivially unit-testable
disadvantages: Zero-division guard returns 0 for 'no data yet', which could be confused with 'genuinely 0% hit rate' by a naive dashboard
common_mistakes: Using stats.total as the denominator -- this includes blocked queries, which deflates the ratio incorrectly
Forgetting the zero-division guard for a freshly-created proxy with no traffic yet
follow_up_questions: Why should blocked queries be excluded from the denominator?
How would this function change if you also wanted to track hit ratio PER query type (A vs AAAA vs others)?
What would a dashboard need to distinguish 'zero traffic yet' from 'genuinely zero hit rate'?

question: Write a small CLI-style function that loads a blocklist file and reports how many domain entries it has.
answer_hinglish:
loadBlockListFile already file-to-string-array parsing deta hai (comments aur blank lines skip karte hue), aur BlockList constructor us array se poori trie build kar deta hai. is function ko sirf dono ko CHAIN karna hai aur BlockList.size property (jo distinct added domains count karta hai, subdomains NAHI) report karna hai.

Yeh function ek CLI tool ka core logic hai -- real CLI mein isko `process.argv[2]` se path lena hoga aur console.log se result print karna hoga, par core logic (load + count) yahan isolate hai testing ke liye. size property specifically 'kitni baar add() se NAYI entry mark hui' count karta hai -- duplicate lines (agar blocklist file mein galti se repeat ho) double-count nahi hongi, kyunki add() `if (!node.blocked)` check karta hai before incrementing count.
why_needed: Interviewer dekhna chahta hai ki candidate existing public API (loadBlockListFile, BlockList, size) ko correctly CHAIN kar sakta hai bina internal implementation detail (jaise trie structure) mein jaaye.
real_world_analogy: Ek inventory count tool jo warehouse ki list file padh ke batata hai 'kitne distinct items hain' -- duplicate entries ko double count nahi karta.
how_it_works: loadBlockListFile text file ko readFileSync se padhta hai aur parseBlockListText se comments/blank lines skip karte hue ek string array banata hai; BlockList constructor us array ke har entry par add() call karta hai, jo duplicate entries ko count mein double nahi karta.
in_this_project: src/blocklist.ts ka loadBlockListFile aur BlockList.size yeh exact public API hai jo yeh exercise use karti hai -- koi internal trie detail touch nahi hota.
advantages: Reuses existing public API exactly as exported -- no new parsing logic needed
size counts distinct domains, correctly ignoring duplicate lines
disadvantages: Does not report how many TOTAL subdomains are implicitly covered (that number is unbounded/not meaningful to compute)
common_mistakes: Counting lines in the file directly instead of using BlockList.size -- this would double-count duplicate or malformed lines that parseBlockListText might still include
Forgetting that size counts distinct domains ADDED, not subdomains covered
follow_up_questions: What would size report if the same domain appeared twice in the file?
How would you report the trie's actual node count (a proxy for memory usage) instead of domain count?
What happens if the file path does not exist -- what does loadBlockListFile do?

question: Write a test proving a cached entry's TTL counts down correctly between two reads separated by a clock advance.
answer_hinglish:
Yeh test ResponseCache ke TTL-countdown behavior ko verify karta hai -- jo cache.ts ka sabse important rule hai (same philosophy jo README ki cache table mein 'countdown test, including right at the edge of expiry' line describe karti hai). ManualClock use karna zaroori hai taaki test deterministic ho, real setTimeout/sleep ki zaroorat na ho.

Steps: (1) ManualClock(0) se shuru karo, cache ko yeh clock do. (2) ek A-record response buffer banao encodeMessage + encodeARecord se, aur decodeResponse se uske ttlOffsets extract karo (yeh exactly woh step hai jo proxy.ts handle() mein karta hai cache.put() call karne se pehle). (3) cache.put() karo 300-second TTL ke saath. (4) pehla cache.get() karo, decode karo, assert karo ttl === 300 (koi time nahi beeta abhi). (5) clock.advance(10_000) karo (10 second). (6) doosra cache.get() karo, decode karo, assert karo ttl === 290.

Yeh test proves karta hai ki get() EACH call par FRESH countdown compute karta hai based on insertedAt se elapsed time, na ki ek STATIC pre-computed value.
why_needed: Interviewer dekhna chahta hai ki candidate TTL-countdown jaisi TIME-DEPENDENT behavior ko DETERMINISTICALLY test kar sakta hai, ManualClock jaisa injectable-clock pattern use karte hue, bina real sleeps ke.
real_world_analogy: Ek parking meter jo har baar check karne par BAKI TIME dikhata hai -- 10 minute pehle 60 minute tha, abhi check karo toh 50 minute dikhega, bina meter ko manually reset kiye.
how_it_works: cache.put() insertedAt ko clock.now() se record karta hai. cache.get() har call par `elapsedSeconds = floor((now - insertedAt) / 1000)` compute karta hai aur har ttlOffset par original TTL se yeh elapsedSeconds subtract karta hai (floored at zero) -- isliye do consecutive get() calls, agar beech mein clock advance hui ho, do ALAG countdown values dengi.
in_this_project: test/cache.test.ts mein already exactly yeh kism ke countdown tests hain (README table reference karti hai 'countdown test, including right at the edge of expiry'); yeh exercise us PATTERN ko reproduce karti hai ManualClock, ResponseCache, aur wire.ts helpers use karte hue.
advantages: Deterministic -- no real sleeps, uses ManualClock exactly like the project's own tests do
Exercises the real decode->cache->decode round trip, not a mocked shortcut
disadvantages: A bit verbose to set up a full encoded message just to test one countdown behavior -- unavoidable given the raw-bytes cache design
common_mistakes: Using systemClock and a real setTimeout instead of ManualClock.advance() -- makes the test slow and flaky
Forgetting to re-extract ttlOffsets from a freshly-decoded buffer before calling put() -- these offsets are what makes the countdown patch land on the right bytes
follow_up_questions: What would this test need to change to verify the countdown floors at zero rather than going negative?
Why must ttlOffsets be computed by decoding the SAME buffer that gets cached?
How would you test that a SECOND, unrelated client's cache lookup gets an independent countdown?

question: Write a function isBlockedBatch(blockList, names: string[]): boolean[] using only BlockList's public API.
answer_hinglish:
BlockList.isBlocked() already EK name ke liye poora trie-walk karta hai aur boolean return karta hai. Batch version sirf EK array ke har element par SAME isBlocked() call karna hai -- koi naya trie-traversal logic likhne ki zaroorat nahi hai, sirf PUBLIC API ko map() ke through loop karna hai.

Yeh function 'batch' hone se performance improve NAHI hoti (har call still apna independent O(labels) walk karta hai) -- iska REAL benefit sirf ERGONOMIC hai: caller ko ek saath multiple names check karne ka EK CLEAN interface milta hai, jaise 'is batch of outgoing requests mein se kaunse blocked hain'. Agar genuinely performance-critical batch lookup chahiye ho (jaise sabhi names ek SHARED prefix share karte hain), ek alag optimized function likhni padegi jo trie ko ek baar hi traverse kare multiple names ke liye -- par yeh exercise sirf PUBLIC API wrap karne ke baare mein hai.
why_needed: Interviewer dekhna chahta hai ki candidate ek SIMPLE utility function likh sakta hai bina internal implementation (trie) ko touch kiye, sirf EXISTING public method ko correctly reuse karte hue.
real_world_analogy: Ek security guard jo har visitor ka ID CHECK karta hai teaser list ke against -- 'batch check' sirf matlab hai guard ek SAATH 5 logon ki ID check kare, har ek apna independent check hai, koi shortcut nahi.
how_it_works: Array.prototype.map() har name ke liye ek independent isBlocked() call karta hai, jo apna khud ka trie-walk karta hai root se -- koi shared state ya memoization beech mein nahi hoti, har call fully isolated hai.
in_this_project: src/blocklist.ts ka BlockList.isBlocked() yeh exact public method hai jo har element ke liye reuse hoga -- koi naya trie access ya internal field touch nahi hota.
advantages: Trivially correct -- reuses the already-tested isBlocked() for each entry
No internal trie state touched, stays fully decoupled from BlockList's implementation
disadvantages: No performance benefit over calling isBlocked() in a loop yourself -- it's purely an ergonomic wrapper
common_mistakes: Trying to 'optimize' this by reaching into BlockList's private trie fields -- defeats the point of using the public API and couples the caller to internal structure
Assuming batching this way makes lookups faster -- each name still does its own independent O(labels) walk
follow_up_questions: Would batching ever genuinely improve performance here, and under what input shape?
How would you test isBlockedBatch against a mix of blocked, allowed, and malformed names?
What would change if names could contain duplicates -- would you deduplicate before checking?

question: Write a function that computes the SERVFAIL rate from a SinkholeProxy's stats object.
answer_hinglish:
Yeh SINK-129 (cache hit ratio) jaisa hi pattern hai, par denominator different hai. servfail rate ka matlab hai 'kitna PERCENT of ALL queries SERVFAIL mein end hui' -- isliye denominator yahan stats.total hona chahiye, na ki sirf cache-eligible subset (jo cacheHitRatio ke liye sahi tha).

Reason: SERVFAIL blocked queries ke LIYE possible hi nahi hai (blocked path kabhi upstream touch nahi karta, isliye kabhi SERVFAIL nahi hota), par 'total queries ka kitna percent SERVFAIL hua' ek USER-FACING metric hai jo blocked/cache-hit/forwarded/servfail sabko include karna chahiye denominator mein, kyunki yeh batata hai 'overall DNS experience kitna healthy hai', na sirf 'cache-eligible path kitna healthy hai'.
why_needed: Interviewer dekhna chahta hai ki candidate samajhta hai ki DIFFERENT metrics ke liye DIFFERENT denominators sahi ho sakte hain -- yeh ek common mistake point hai jahan candidates galti se same formula sab jagah copy-paste kar dete hain.
real_world_analogy: Ek dukaan ka 'customer complaint rate' sabhi customers ke against measure hota hai (total visitors), na sirf unke against jo kuch khareedne aaye the -- yeh OVERALL experience ka signal hai.
how_it_works: stats.total HAR handle() call par increment hota hai, shuru mein hi, pehle kisi bhi decision se pehle -- isliye yeh TRUE total hai, koi filtered subset nahi. stats.servfail sirf catch block mein increment hota hai jab forward/decode/verify kahin fail ho.
in_this_project: SinkholeProxy.stats.total aur stats.servfail directly yeh calculation ke liye available hain, bina kisi filtering ke.
advantages: Correct denominator (total) for a user-facing health metric
Trivial to export as an alerting threshold in production monitoring
disadvantages: A single aggregate rate hides WHICH domains are failing -- useful as an alert trigger, not a diagnosis tool
common_mistakes: Copy-pasting the cacheHitRatio denominator pattern (cacheHits + forwarded + servfail) here instead of using total -- this would subtly inflate the servfail rate by excluding blocked queries from the denominator
Not guarding against total === 0 for a freshly-started proxy
follow_up_questions: Why is total the right denominator here but not for cacheHitRatio?
What threshold would you alert on for servfailRate in production?
How would you break this rate down by failure cause (timeout vs mismatched reply)?

question: Write a function that mirrors proxy.ts's upstream-reply validation: given the original query buffer and a candidate reply buffer, decide whether the reply's id/QR should be trusted.
answer_hinglish:
proxy.ts ka handle() method upstream se aaya reply decode karne ke baad yeh check karta hai: `if (!parsed.header.qr || parsed.header.id !== rawHeader.id) throw new WireError(...)`. Yeh exercise isi check ko ek STANDALONE, testable function mein extract karta hai -- same logic, par koi throw nahi, seedha boolean return karta hai.

Dono headers decode karne ke liye decodeHeader() use karna hoga (cheap 12-byte peek, poora message decode nahi karna). Agar DONO mein se koi bhi decode fail ho (malformed buffer), function false return kare -- 'invalid' aur 'mismatched' dono untrusted treat hone chahiye. Agar dono decode ho jaayen, check karo reply.qr === true (yeh ek RESPONSE hona chahiye, query nahi) AND reply.id === query.id (transaction correlation match).

Yeh exactly woh invariant hai jo PROXY3 mutation check (README table mein) specifically target karta hai -- is check ke bina, ek buggy ya malicious upstream apna khud ka galat-id wala answer client ko RELAY ho sakta tha.
why_needed: Interviewer dekhna chahta hai ki candidate security-relevant validation logic ko handle() se EXTRACT kar sakta hai ek reusable, testable function mein, bina underlying invariant ko badle.
real_world_analogy: Ek receptionist jo check karta hai ki jo reply aaya hai woh EXACTLY wahi request number carry kare jo bheja gaya tha, aur yeh bhi confirm kare ki yeh ek 'jawab' hai na ki ek NAYA sawal jo galti se wapas aa gaya.
how_it_works: decodeHeader() ek cheap 12-byte peek hai (poora message decode nahi karta). Dono headers decode hone ke baad, sirf do fields compare hote hain: qr (boolean, true hona chahiye kyunki yeh REPLY hai) aur id (query ke id se exactly match karna chahiye) -- dono conditions AND ke saath combine hoti hain.
in_this_project: src/proxy.ts ka handle() method mein `if (!parsed.header.qr || parsed.header.id !== rawHeader.id) throw new WireError("upstream reply did not match our query")` yeh exact check hai jo yeh exercise standalone function mein extract karti hai.
advantages: Extracts a security-relevant check into an isolated, independently testable unit
Treats decode failure and mismatch the same way (both untrusted) -- no special-casing that could be exploited
disadvantages: This standalone function duplicates logic that lives in proxy.ts -- in the real codebase, you would want ONE source of truth, not two copies of this check
common_mistakes: Only checking header.id and forgetting header.qr -- a confused upstream that echoes back the ORIGINAL QUERY (qr=false) with the right id would incorrectly pass
Letting a decode failure propagate as an uncaught exception instead of returning false -- callers expect a boolean, not a thrown error
follow_up_questions: Why must both qr AND id be checked, not just id alone?
How does PROXY3's mutation test prove this check is genuinely exercised?
Would you refactor proxy.ts's handle() to call this extracted function instead of duplicating the logic?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Extracting this check into a standalone function improves testability and reuse, but risks divergence from the real check in proxy.ts if one is updated and not the other -- in a real refactor, handle() should call this extracted function rather than keep an inline duplicate.
advanced.failure_scenarios: If only the id were checked (not qr), a confused upstream that echoes the client's own query back unchanged (same id, qr still false) would pass validation and get relayed as if it were a real answer -- the client would receive something that is not actually a DNS response.
advanced.alternatives: Checking the full question section (name/type/class) matches too, in addition to id/qr, would be stricter but is not what this project does -- id/qr matching is the minimum RFC-expected correlation check, and this project deliberately keeps to that minimum given its narrower threat model.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: This is a per-packet correctness check with negligible cost (two 12-byte header decodes); it does not change with traffic volume.
advanced.production_improvements: If this logic were extracted for reuse, replace the inline check in proxy.ts's handle() with a call to this function, and add a dedicated unit test suite for it separate from proxy.test.ts's end-to-end style tests.

question: Sketch a small in-flight request coalescer class that could be used to dedupe concurrent identical upstream forwards, as discussed in the request-coalescing design question.
answer_hinglish:
Yeh exercise SINK-124 ke design discussion ko ACTUAL code mein implement karta hai -- ek generic, reusable `InFlightCoalescer` class jo KISI BHI async operation ko key-based dedupe kar sake, is project ke specific DNS types se decoupled.

Core idea: ek `Map<string, Promise<T>>` jo 'currently running' operations track kare. `run(key, fetcher)` call hone par, agar key already map mein hai, EXISTING promise return karo (join karo). Agar nahi hai, `fetcher()` call karo, result ko map mein DAALO IMMEDIATELY (await se pehle), aur `.finally()` se map se REMOVE karo jab woh settle ho jaaye (success YA failure dono mein) -- yeh zaroori hai taaki ek FAILED fetch bhi cleanup ho, aur agla genuine attempt STALE rejected promise na pakde.

Is project mein use karne ke liye, SinkholeProxy ek InFlightCoalescer<Buffer> instance rakhega, aur forwardQuery() call ko `coalescer.run(canonicalKey, () => forwardQuery(...))` se wrap karega -- yeh SINK-124 mein diya gaya concrete design hai, bas yahan generic reusable class ke roop mein extracted hai.
why_needed: Interviewer dekhna chahta hai ki candidate ek GENERIC, reusable concurrency-control utility likh sakta hai (not DNS-specific), aur cleanup correctness (finally block, success+failure dono) ko sahi se handle karta hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek elevator jo already EK direction mein chal raha hai -- agar koi aur button dabaye SAME floor ke liye jahan elevator already jaa raha hai, unhe NAYA elevator call nahi karna padta, woh EXISTING trip ka wait kar sakte hain.
how_it_works: run(key, fetcher) pehle map mein key check karta hai -- mila toh EXISTING promise seedha return (join). Nahi mila toh fetcher() call hoti hai, result-promise IMMEDIATELY map mein set hoti hai (await se pehle, race avoid karne ke liye), aur `.finally()` attach hota hai jo promise settle hone par (resolve YA reject dono) map se entry hata deta hai.
in_this_project: Yeh class is repo mein abhi NAHI hai -- yeh SINK-124 ke 'request coalescing' Advanced design question ka EXTENSION hai, jo src/proxy.ts ke forwardQuery() call ke around wrap ho sakta hai agar yeh feature add ki jaaye.
advantages: Generic over T -- reusable beyond just DNS forwarding, decoupled from this project's specific types
Cleanup via .finally() handles both success and failure, avoiding a stale-promise leak
disadvantages: Does not itself solve the 'different callers need different patched output' problem (e.g. transaction-id patching) -- that must still happen AFTER joining the shared promise
In-memory, single-process only -- does not coalesce across multiple proxy instances
common_mistakes: Deleting the map entry only inside a .then() (success path) instead of .finally() -- a failed fetch would leave a stale rejected promise blocking future genuine attempts for that key
Setting the map entry AFTER awaiting fetcher() instead of before -- this reopens the race window the coalescer is meant to close
follow_up_questions: Why must the map entry be set before awaiting the fetcher, not after?
How would SinkholeProxy.handle() need to change to use this coalescer around forwardQuery?
What test would prove two concurrent identical queries result in only one call to the underlying fetcher?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: A generic coalescer class is more reusable than inlining the Map directly into SinkholeProxy, at the cost of one extra layer of indirection to understand.
advanced.failure_scenarios: If cleanup happened only on success, a burst of identical queries during an upstream outage would have their FIRST attempt fail, but then get stuck: the stale rejected promise would keep being returned to every subsequent caller for that key until it was manually cleared, even after the upstream recovered.
advanced.alternatives: A TTL-based coalescing window (hold the promise slot for a few ms even after it settles, to catch near-simultaneous but not perfectly concurrent callers) is more aggressive but adds complexity and a new tunable parameter.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: This coalescer's benefit scales with how CONCURRENT identical queries are -- at low concurrency it does little, but during a traffic spike for one popular domain it can turn N simultaneous upstream calls into 1.
advanced.production_improvements: Add a counter tracking how many times run() joined an existing promise vs started a new fetch, to measure how often coalescing actually helps in real traffic.

question: Why does the allowlist win unconditionally, regardless of specificity, instead of using a most-specific-match-wins rule?
answer_hinglish:
Direct answer: humne Pi-hole ka documented behaviour match kiya -- allowlist mein match hua toh naam block nahi hoga, chahe matching block entry zyada specific ho ya kam. Yeh ek real choice thi, non-choice nahi; most-specific-wins bhi defensible hai.

Teen reasons. Pehla, migration expectation: jo operator Pi-hole se aa raha hai, woh yahi expect karega. Doosra, implementation cost: 'kya yeh naam allowlist ko match karta hai' wahi single trie walk hai jo BlockList.isBlocked() pehle se karta hai, toh handle() mein bas `const allowed = this.allowList?.isBlocked(name) ?? false;` aur `if (!allowed && this.blockList.isBlocked(name))` -- do lines. Most-specific-wins ke liye dono tries ko END tak walk karna padta (isBlocked() abhi pehle marked node par early-return karta hai), har ek ka deepest matching depth nikalna padta, aur compare karna padta -- naya code, naya bug ka rasta. Teesra, explainability: most-specific-wins mein ek narrow 'allow this one subdomain' entry chupchaap kisi baad mein add hue broad block se haar sakti hai ya jeet sakti hai depending on depth -- yeh support question banta hai, feature nahi.

Cost bhi honestly batana chahiye: allow-always-wins mein 'example.com allow karo par ads.example.com phir bhi block rakho' express nahi ho sakta. Test 'a broader ALLOWED parent beats a narrower BLOCKED subdomain too' exactly yahi behaviour lock karta hai -- toh yeh accidental nahi, documented aur tested hai.
why_needed: Precedence rules har policy system (firewalls, ad blockers, IAM) mein aate hain; interviewer dekhta hai ki tum ek rule choose karke uski cost bhi bata sakte ho, sirf 'jo intuitive lage' nahi.
real_world_analogy: Ek building mein 'VIP pass' system: VIP pass hai toh har restricted floor khul jaata hai, guard yeh compare nahi karta ki restriction floor-level thi ya room-level. Simple, predictable -- par 'VIP ho par server room phir bhi band' express karne ka tareeka nahi.
how_it_works: isBlocked() reversed labels par walk karta hai aur pehle marked node par true return karta hai. Allowlist ke liye yahi call kaafi hai kyunki humein sirf 'koi bhi ancestor-or-self allowlisted hai?' poochna hai. Agar true, blockList.isBlocked() call hi nahi hota (`!allowed &&` short-circuit). Specificity kabhi compute nahi hoti.
in_this_project: src/proxy.ts handle() mein comment explicitly kehta hai: allowlist checked FIRST aur 'wins unconditionally', narrower allowed subdomain broader blocked parent ko beat karta hai AND broader allowed parent narrower blocked subdomain ko. test/proxy.test.ts "allowlist (Stage 2)" mein dono directions ke tests hain ('safe.ads.example.com' vs 'ads.example.com', aur 'example.com' vs 'ads.example.com'). PLAN.md 'Stage 2 decisions' mein yeh reasoning likhi hai. Mutation ALLOW7 (blocklist pehle check, allowlist baad mein) caught hua.
advantages: Ek trie walk, do lines code -- galat implement karne ki jagah kam
Pi-hole users ke liye familiar, explain karna ek sentence mein
isBlocked() ka early-return optimisation dono lists par chalta rehta hai
disadvantages: Broad allow ke andar ek specific block express nahi ho sakta
Ek galti se broad allowlist entry (jaise 'com') poora blocklist disable kar sakti hai -- koi warning nahi
common_mistakes: Sochna ki allowlist sirf narrower entries ke liye kaam karta hai -- test prove karta hai broader allow bhi jeet-ta hai
Most-specific-wins ko free samajhna -- isBlocked() ka early return chhodna padta aur depth comparison likhna padta
Allowlist check ko blocklist ke BAAD rakhna (ALLOW7 mutation) -- tab allowlist kabhi kaam hi nahi karta
follow_up_questions: Most-specific-wins chahiye ho toh BlockList mein kaunsa naya method add karoge?
Ek dangerous broad allowlist entry (jaise ek TLD) ko load time par kaise detect karoge?
Firewall rules (first-match) aur yeh rule kaise alag hain?

question: Why is the allowlist a second instance of the existing BlockList class rather than a new AllowList class or an allow-mode flag on BlockList?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki BlockList ka trie already EXACTLY wahi matching rule deta hai jo allowlist ko chahiye -- exact domain plus har subdomain -- aur uska isBlocked() method asal mein 'kya yeh naam is list ki kisi entry ko match karta hai' hai. Match ka MATLAB (block karo ya allow karo) data structure mein nahi, caller mein rehta hai: SinkholeProxy.handle().

Mode flag add karna ek class ko do kaam deta: trie walk karna AUR yeh jaanna ki match ka kya matlab hai -- zero benefit ke saath, kyunki trie code dono uses mein ek byte bhi nahi badalta. Naya AllowList class banana duplicate code hota (ya ek thin wrapper jo kuch add nahi karta). Isi wajah se parser bhi reuse hua: config/allowlist.txt ko parseBlockListText/loadBlockListFile as-is padhte hain, same format (ek domain per line, # aur ; comments).

Doosra bada fayda backward compatibility: `allowList?: BlockList` optional hai, aur `this.allowList?.isBlocked(name) ?? false` ka matlab hai bina allowlist ke code path bilkul Stage 1 jaisa -- koi 'kya allowlist hai bhi?' branch alag se nahi. Saare Stage 1 tests bina modification pass hue, aur ek dedicated test 'a proxy constructed with NO allowlist configured behaves identically to Stage 1' isse lock karta hai.

Honest cost: naam thoda misleading hai -- allowlist par `isBlocked()` call karna padhne mein ajeeb lagta hai. PLAN.md aur proxy.ts ka doc comment yeh explicitly explain karte hain. Ek rename (jaise `matches()`) cleaner hota, par woh Stage 1 API todta.
why_needed: Yeh 'composition vs flags' aur 'data structure vs policy' ka classic design sawaal hai -- interviewer dekhta hai tum naya class tab banate ho jab zaroorat ho, reflex se nahi.
real_world_analogy: Ek hi tarah ki register-book do jagah use hoti hai: gate par 'banned visitors' ke liye aur 'pre-approved visitors' ke liye. Register same hai, naam dhoondhne ka tareeka same; guard decide karta hai ki naam milne ka matlab kya hai. Register mein 'mode' likhne ki zaroorat nahi.
how_it_works: proxy.ts mein `import type { BlockList }` hai aur dono fields `blockList: BlockList` aur `allowList?: BlockList` same type ke hain. Caller dono ko `new BlockList(loadBlockListFile(...))` se banata hai. handle() pehle allowList par isBlocked() chalata hai, phir (agar allowed nahi) blockList par -- same method, opposite meaning.
in_this_project: src/proxy.ts SinkholeProxyOptions ka `allowList?: BlockList` doc comment kehta hai 'it is the identical BlockList class, just holding a different set of names'. src/blocklist.ts Stage 2 mein unchanged raha. README ka usage example `allowList: new BlockList(loadBlockListFile("config/allowlist.txt"))` dikhata hai. Test 'loading a real allowlist file end to end' config/allowlist.txt ko loadBlockListFile se load karke 'allowed.ads.example.com' forward hona prove karta hai.
advantages: Zero new trie/parser code -- Stage 1 ke 14 blocklist tests allowlist matching ko bhi cover karte hain
Optional field + optional chaining = backward compatible bina extra branch
Policy (match ka matlab) ek jagah, handle() mein
disadvantages: `allowList.isBlocked()` naam padhne mein misleading hai
Type system allowlist aur blocklist ko swap karne se nahi rokta -- ALLOW4 mutation (allowed ko blockList se compute karna) sirf tests ne pakda, compiler ne nahi
common_mistakes: Har naye 'concept' ke liye naya class bana dena jab behaviour identical ho
Mode flag ko 'flexible' samajhna -- woh har method mein `if (mode === ...)` branches laata hai
Optional allowList ke liye non-null assertion (`!`) use karna -- ALLOW6 mutation ne dikhaya yeh bina allowlist ke throw karta
follow_up_questions: Agar type-level guarantee chahiye ki dono lists swap na hon, kya branded types use karoge?
isBlocked() ko rename karna ho toh backward compatibility kaise maintain karoge?
Kab ek alag AllowList class justified ho jaati (jaise agar allowlist regex support kare)?

question: Mutation ALLOW10 (passing the raw q.name instead of the canonicalized name to the allowlist lookup) survived the whole suite. How did you decide it was an equivalent mutant rather than a missing test, and what is the catch?
answer_hinglish:
Equivalent mutant woh hota hai jo code badalta hai par observable behaviour NAHI -- koi test usse pakad hi nahi sakta, kyunki pakadne layak kuch hai hi nahi. Survivor aane par pehla sawaal 'kaunsa test missing hai' nahi, balki 'kya yeh mutation behaviour badalta bhi hai' hona chahiye.

ALLOW10 ke liye maine dono paths trace kiye. Original: `canonicalName(q.name)` (lowercase + ek trailing dot strip) phir `allowList.isBlocked(name)`. Mutant: seedha `allowList.isBlocked(q.name)`. Lekin isBlocked() khud labelsOf() call karta hai, jo trim, toLowerCase aur ek trailing dot strip karta hai. Toh canonicalize karke dena aur raw dena -- dono same labels banate hain. Isliye README/PLAN mein yeh 'equivalent mutant, not a real gap' record hua, ek fake test likhne ki jagah jo bas pass ho jaata.

Catch (yeh interview mein bolna strong lagta hai): 'har possible input' par strictly equivalent nahi hai. wire.ts labels ko latin1 strings rakhta hai aur presentation escapes support nahi karta, toh ek crafted query jiska last label literal '.' bytes par khatam ho (decode hone par naam jaise 'x.com..') do baar strip hota hai original path mein (canonicalName phir labelsOf) par mutant mein ek hi baar -- aur labelsOf empty label par RangeError throw karta hai. Yeh input class PLAN.md mein already out of scope hai ('a label containing a literal "." byte'), isliye practically equivalent kehna fair hai -- par precise claim yeh hai: 'supported input domain par equivalent'. Agar kabhi wire.ts escapes support kare, ALLOW10 dobara dekhna padega.
why_needed: Mutation testing ka sabse common confusion equivalent mutants hai. Interviewer dekhta hai ki tum survivor ko blindly test se 'close' karte ho ya reasoning se classify karte ho -- aur us reasoning ki limits jaante ho.
real_world_analogy: Ek letter do baar envelope mein daalna vs ek baar -- agar post office waise bhi bahar ka envelope khol deta hai, toh receiver ko farak nahi padta. Par agar koi ajeeb letter aaye jisme andar teen envelope hon, toh 'farak nahi padta' wala claim toot sakta hai.
how_it_works: canonicalName = asciiLower + `.replace(/\.$/, "")`. labelsOf = trim + toLowerCase + `.replace(/\.$/, "")` + split + empty-label check. Normal names par f(canonical(x)) == f(x) kyunki lowercase idempotent hai aur ek-trailing-dot strip sirf ek baar zaroori hai. Do trailing dots wale naam par canonical path dono dots hata deta, raw path ek chhod deta jisse split mein empty label aata hai.
in_this_project: README.md 'Stage 2 mutation checks' table: ALLOW10 'not caught -- equivalent mutant, not a real gap'; 11 checks, 10 caught. PLAN.md 'Stage 2 decisions' ka last bullet yahi reasoning record karta hai. src/blocklist.ts ka labelsOf aur src/wire.ts ka canonicalName woh do functions hain jinke overlap se equivalence aati hai. src/wire.ts ka file header 'No RFC 1035 presentation escapes' wala scope cut edge case ko out of scope rakhta hai.
advantages: Fake test likhne se bacha -- suite mein har test kuch real prove karta hai
Reasoning docs mein recorded hai, agla developer wahi investigation dobara nahi karega
disadvantages: Equivalence ek human argument hai, machine-checked nahi -- edge cases miss ho sakte hain (jaise double-dot case)
Agar baad mein labelsOf ka normalisation badla, ALLOW10 chupchaap real gap ban sakta hai
common_mistakes: Har survivor ke liye turant test likhna, bina check kiye ki mutation observable hai
'Equivalent' ko 'har input par identical' bolna jab sach mein 'supported inputs par identical' ho
Canonicalization ko do jagah karna aur sochna ki ek hata do toh kuch nahi hoga -- defence-in-depth ka matlab redundancy hi hai
follow_up_questions: Kya tum ek test likhoge jo double-dot label par mutant aur original ko alag kare, ya input ko wire.ts mein hi reject karoge?
Automated tools (Stryker) equivalent mutants ko kaise handle karte hain?
Blocklist lookup bhi canonical name use karta hai -- kya wahan bhi same equivalence hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Normalising in two layers (canonicalName in the proxy, labelsOf inside BlockList) makes BlockList safe to call with any string, but it also makes the outer normalisation redundant for lookups -- which is exactly what turns a mutation of it into a near-equivalent mutant.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Mutant ke saath ek crafted query jiska last label '..' par khatam ho, handle() se RangeError bahar phenk sakti thi (isBlocked() handle() ke try/catch ke bahar call hota hai). Original code mein yeh nahi hota kyunki canonicalName ek dot pehle hi hata deta hai.
advanced.alternatives: wire.ts mein decode ke waqt '.' byte wale labels ko FORMERR se reject karna -- tab ALLOW10 sach mein har accepted input par equivalent ho jaata; ya labelsOf ko trailing dots ki poori run strip karne dena.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Codebase 10x hone par manual equivalence reasoning scale nahi karti; automated mutation tools hundreds of survivors denge, jinme se kaafi equivalent honge -- unhe triage karne ke liye clear 'supported input domain' documentation zaroori hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Equivalent mutants ka ek list README mein rakhna (jaise abhi hai) aur us list ko input-domain assumptions se link karna, taaki wire.ts ka scope badle toh yeh re-check trigger ho.

question: Why is ProxyStats.allowed a separate counter that is incremented alongside cacheHits/forwarded, instead of its own exclusive bucket like blocked or servfail?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki `allowed` aur `forwarded` alag operator sawaalon ka jawab dete hain. `forwarded` kehta hai 'kitni queries upstream tak gayi'. `allowed` kehta hai 'kitni queries ne EXPLICITLY allowlist match kiya, yaani kitni baar allowlist ne blocklist ko override kiya (ya override karne ka mauka tha)'. Ek query jo kabhi blocklist par thi hi nahi, woh `forwarded` mein aati hai par `allowed` mein NAHI.

Yeh exclusive bucket kyun nahi? Kyunki allowlisted query ka safar wahi rehta hai jo kisi normal non-blocked query ka: woh cache check karti hai, hit ho toh cacheHits++, miss ho toh forward aur forwarded++ (ya fail ho toh servfail++). `allowed` ek EXTRA tag hai, outcome nahi. `blocked` aur `servfail` outcomes hain -- query wahin khatam hoti hai -- isliye woh exclusive hain.

Practical use: ek operator ne allowlist mein entry daali aur poochta hai 'kya yeh kuch kar bhi rahi hai?'. Bina `allowed` ke, stats se yeh pata hi nahi chalta -- forwarded toh waise bhi badhta. Test 'stats.allowed counts allowlist-overridden queries, distinct from forwarded/cacheHits' chaar queries bhejta hai aur assert karta hai `{ total: 4, allowed: 2, blocked: 1, forwarded: 2, cacheHits: 1 }` -- dekho, allowed + blocked + forwarded + cacheHits total se zyada hai, aur woh sahi hai. Isliye ratios banate waqt `allowed` ko outcomes ke saath jodna galti hai.
why_needed: Metrics design ka basic sawaal: koi counter OUTCOME hai (mutually exclusive) ya ATTRIBUTE (overlapping). Galat samjha toh dashboards ke ratios galat aate hain.
real_world_analogy: Ek dukaan mein 'kitne customers ne kuch khareeda' aur 'kitne customers ne discount coupon use kiya' -- coupon wala customer bhi khareedne wale count mein hai. Coupon count ek alag tag hai, alag customer category nahi.
how_it_works: handle() mein `const allowed = this.allowList?.isBlocked(name) ?? false; if (allowed) this.stats.allowed++;` block check se pehle chalta hai. Phir code aage normal path par jaata hai, jahan cacheHits++ ya forwarded++ ya servfail++ hota hai. Isliye ek allowlisted query exactly do counters badhati hai (total ko chhod ke).
in_this_project: src/proxy.ts ProxyStats ka doc comment kehta hai `allowed` 'counted SEPARATELY from -- and alongside -- cacheHits/forwarded' aur 'A query that was simply never on the blocklist is NOT counted here'. Mutations ALLOW2 (increment hataya), ALLOW8 (allowed ki jagah blocked++), aur ALLOW11 (if (allowed) guard hataya -- har query count hone lagi) teeno caught hue.
advantages: Allowlist entries ka asar directly measurable
Existing cache-hit-ratio / servfail-rate formulas bina change ke sahi rehte hain
disadvantages: Counters ka sum total ke barabar nahi hota -- naye reader ko confuse kar sakta hai
`allowed` yeh nahi batata ki allowlist ne ACTUALLY ek block override kiya ya naam blocklist par tha hi nahi (allowlisted par blocklist se bahar naam bhi count hota hai)
common_mistakes: allowed + blocked + forwarded + cacheHits + servfail ko total ke barabar expect karna
Cache hit ratio ke denominator mein `allowed` jodna -- double counting
Har non-blocked query ko 'allowed' kehna -- yahan allowed ka matlab sirf allowlist match hai
follow_up_questions: Agar sirf 'allowlist ne kitne REAL blocks override kiye' chahiye, toh kaunsa naya counter aur kahan increment karoge?
Prometheus mein yeh counters labels ke saath kaise model karoge (outcome label vs allowlisted label)?

question: Write tests proving the allowlist override is scoped correctly: an allowlisted subdomain of a blocked parent is forwarded, while a sibling under the same blocked parent is still blocked.
answer_hinglish:
Do tests chahiye, aur dono zaroori hain kyunki ek akela test ek bug chhupa sakta hai. Pehla test: blocked = ['ads.example.com'], allowed = ['safe.ads.example.com'], query 'safe.ads.example.com' -> NOERROR aur stub.callCount 1 (upstream tak gaya). Yeh prove karta hai ki override kaam karta hai.

Par sirf yeh test ek ulta bug pass hone deta: agar implementation galti se allowlist match ko 'poore parent ko unblock karo' samajh le, ya allowlist ko suffix ki jagah kisi aur tarah match kare, toh pehla test phir bhi green hoga. Isliye doosra test: same lists, query 'other.ads.example.com' -> NXDOMAIN aur stub.callCount 0. Yeh prove karta hai ki override sirf allowlisted naam ki APNI subtree tak scoped hai.

Assertions mein dono cheezein check karo: rcode (client ko kya mila) AUR stub.callCount (upstream ko call hua ya nahi). Sirf rcode check karna kamzor hai -- ek bug jo upstream ko call karke phir NXDOMAIN de, rcode test pass kar dega par privacy promise tod dega ('blocked query never reaches upstream').

Is project ke test/proxy.test.ts mein yahi dono tests exist karte hain 'allowlist (Stage 2)' describe block mein, existing harness() helper ke saath jo `allowed` option ko `new BlockList(opts.allowed)` mein badalta hai. Mutations ALLOW3 (`!allowed &&` guard hataya) aur ALLOW9 (`&&` ko `||` banaya) inhi jaise tests se pakde gaye.
why_needed: Positive aur negative dono cases ke saath scoping test likhna ek basic test-design skill hai -- interviewer dekhta hai ki tum sirf happy path test karte ho ya boundary bhi.
real_world_analogy: Ek naya chaabi-card test karna: sirf yeh check karna kaafi nahi ki tumhara room khulta hai -- yeh bhi check karo ki bagal wala room NAHI khulta.
how_it_works: harness() ek StubUpstream start karta hai aur SinkholeProxy banata hai `blockList: new BlockList(opts.blocked ?? [])` aur `allowList: opts.allowed ? new BlockList(opts.allowed) : undefined` ke saath. proxy.handle(buildQuery(...)) seedha call hota hai (socket nahi), reply decodeResponse se parse hota hai, aur stub.callCount upstream calls ginta hai.
in_this_project: test/proxy.test.ts: 'a domain whose PARENT is blocklisted but the domain itself is allowlisted is forwarded (specific override)' aur 'a sibling subdomain NOT on the allowlist, under the same blocklisted parent, is still blocked'. Demo (src/demo.ts) bhi yahi do cases console par dikhata hai. Solution neeche real tests hain (trimmed nahi).
advantages: Positive + negative pair bugs ko dono directions mein pakadta hai
stub.callCount se privacy guarantee (blocked never reaches upstream) bhi verify hoti hai
disadvantages: Sirf ek level deep scenario -- 'x.safe.ads.example.com' (allowlisted naam ka subdomain) explicitly test nahi hai
common_mistakes: Sirf override wala positive test likhna
Sirf rcode assert karna, upstream call count nahi
Har test ke liye real UDP server chalana jab handle() seedha call ho sakta hai
follow_up_questions: Allowlisted naam ke subdomain (x.safe.ads.example.com) ke liye kya expect karoge, aur kyun?
Yahi guarantee invariant.test.ts jaise randomized test mein kaise add karoge?
